docs.title: The Philosophy
docs.text:
When I was in high school, I was the captain of the calculator team. My instrument of choice was a legendary tactile Reverse Polish Notation scientific calculator. It was fast, mechanical, and mathematically pure. For years afterward, throughout engineering school and research, I relied on postfix evaluation, always missing the physical immediacy of that tactile machine.

When my daughter started middle school and was finally allowed to use a calculator in class, I looked for an everyday, accessible RPN handheld for her. There were none. The market offered only two extremes: fragile, expensive vintage collectibles suited for display cases, or disposable in-fix graphing bricks covered in confusing parentheses syntax and battery compartments that corrode.

So I built my own.

StackCalc is not a retro novelty or a piece designed to sit behind glass for collectors. It is designed to be a fast, everyday mathematical instrument that you reach for when you need to solve real-world problems. Our mission is simple: end the cognitive friction of in-fix entry, unbind learners from the confusion of nested parentheses, and eliminate the forced equals sign once and for all.

  • Native Watch & Phone Digital Twin: Immediate access on modern everyday devices. It provides a tactile gateway to learn RPN before graduating to the dedicated hardware instrument.
  • Interactive Tutorials: Built-in guided learning modules demonstrating how the four-level stack evaluates expressions sequentially without syntax errors.
  • Deliberate Minimalism & Focus: We removed features common to distracting classroom devices for intentional pedagogical reasons:
  • No Complex Scripting: Kept intentionally non-programmable so it is fully compliant with ACT, SAT, and AP exam testing regulations.
  • No Radios or Touchscreen Distractions: Hardware firmware contains zero Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or camera hardware, ensuring 100% exam compliance and unbreakable classroom focus.
  • No CAS Black Boxes: Solvers are strictly numeric and evaluate via visible stack steps.
  • No Unwieldy Matrix Menus: Deep matrix algebra belongs on modern computational notebooks; everyday calculation belongs on an immediate, tactile handheld.

Geek out over the details with us. Welcome to StackCalc32.

docs.title: 1. Sourcing Strategy: In-House Printing vs. Slant3D for Batch 001
Strategic Recommendation: The "In-House Pilot → Slant3D Farm Scale" Hybrid Model
docs.text:
Executive Summary: Print Batch 001 (5 units per SKU: 1 studio master copy + 4 ready-to-ship boxed copies) IN-HOUSE. Do not outsource Batch 001 completely to Slant3D. Maintain full in-house control over the inaugural release, then transition high-volume, single-material components to Slant3D once sales velocity is established.

                    BATCH 001 (LAUNCH & PILOT)             BATCH 002+ (SCALE)
┌──────────────────┐  In-House High-Precision Printing      In-House Assembly & QA
│ SC-32 Calculator │ ─────────────────────────────────► ─────────────────────────────►

│                  │  • Archimedean micro-groove faceplate  • Multi-material faceplates

│ Math             │ ─────────────────────────────────► ─────────────────────────────►
│ Manipulatives    │  • 10-20 units per SKU                 • High-volume PLA printing

docs.title: Detailed Engineering & Economic Comparison
docs.text: Strategic Dimension In-House 3D Printing (Batch 001) Direct Slant3D Sourcing (Batch 001) Winner for Batch 001 Mechanical Tolerances High Precision (\(0.20\,\text{mm}\) dovetails): Calibrated on tuned Bambu/Prusa machines. Tool-free sliding rails glide smoothly without binding or slop. Standard Industrial (\(0.40–0.60\,\text{mm}\)): Slant3D uses high-flow production nozzles; tight sliding tongue-and-groove joints can bind or require manual post-cleanup. In-House Multi-Material / CMF Full CMF Capability: Can print Shore 95A flexible TPU membranes, anisotropic silk PLAs, frosted optical PETG, and Archimedean spiral concentric toolpaths. Single-Material PLA/PETG: Slant3D farm lines do not support multi-material TPU co-molding, special silk gradients, or laser foil inlays. In-House Inventory & Cash Risk Zero Upfront Inventory: Print on-demand or keep 5–10 kits boxed on the shelf. Zero capital tied up in unsold units. Batch MOQ / Setup Overhead: Outsourcing small test runs incurs setup fees, shipping freight, and MOQ constraints. In-House Rapid Iteration Cycle Immediate (10 minutes): If an early customer reports a fraction block or algebra tile is 0.1mm too snug, you modify the OpenSCAD code and print the corrected part immediately. Slow (2–4 weeks): Re-uploading CAD, queueing at the farm, batch fabrication, and ground freight back to your shop. In-House First Review Reputation Boutique Surface Finish: Textured PEI plates, dialed retraction (\(0.98\) flow), and hand-checked snap retention generate enthusiastic 5-star Etsy reviews. Factory Finish: Quality is consistent for volume parts, but lacks the hand-inspected artisan feel needed for early Listing Quality Score (LQS). In-House High-Volume Unit Cost Higher labor cost per unit if scaled past 100 units/month. Lowest Cost at Scale: Robotic automated ejection and bulk filament pricing dominate at \(>100\) units. Slant3D (Scale)

docs.title: When to Trigger the Slant3D Hand-Off (Batch 002+ Milestone)
docs.text: Transition parts to Slant3D when: 1. Steady Velocity: A manipulative SKU sells \(>20\) units per month, or a school district places a PO for \(>10\) classroom kits (\(>150\) total trays/boxes). 2. Stable Geometry: The OpenSCAD CAD code has zero geometry adjustments across 30 days of classroom feedback. 3. Component Suitability: Outsource the monolithic, high-part-count components (e.g. Fraction Studio towers, Gridfinity boxes, Ten-Frame carry shelves) while continuing to assemble, QA, and package in-house with the SC-32 electronics.

docs.title: 4. Git Hash Tracking & 50% Anti-Arbitrage Replacement Workflow
4.1 The 50% Anti-Arbitrage Pricing Formula
docs.text:
To prevent customers or third parties from buying individual components to assemble full kits piecemeal, all replacement parts are priced at 50% above the amortized per-piece price of the full retail kit (\(1.5 \times \text{Amortized Cost}\)): - Small Tile / Counter / Single Domino Tile: $2.49 (Amortized $1.66) - Trio Small Tiles / Domino 6-Pack: $3.99 – $6.75 (Amortized $2.66–$4.50) - Linear Rod / Medium Tower: $3.49 – $4.95 (Amortized $2.33–$3.30) - Quadrant Wedge / Clock Hand: $5.25 – $6.00 (Amortized $3.50–$4.00) - 12-Frame Math Tray / Doubling Lid / Quadratic x² Tile: $6.49 – $7.50 (Amortized $4.33–$5.00) - Whole Block / 3x1x7U Storage Box / Complete Stand: $11.25 – $22.50 (Amortized $7.50–$15.00) - Planetary Gear Core / SC-32 Bezel: $18.00 – $24.00 (Amortized $12.00–$16.00)

Anti-Arbitrage Result: Assembling an entire kit piecemeal costs \(>2.2\times\) the boxed retail price, eliminating part-out arbitrage while keeping single-piece replacement affordable for honest classrooms.

docs.title: 4.2 Automated Git Content-Addressed Manifest Tracking (Zero Version Churn)
docs.text:
A common concern with Git-based versioning is: "Does every commit to the repository bump the version of all physical parts?" No. We eliminate global version churn by leveraging Git's fundamental content-addressing architecture:

  1. Git Content Blob Hashes (git hash-object):
  2. The primary ID for every STL model is its Git Blob SHA (e.g., 0bf1e7f for algebra_factoring_box.stl).
  3. This SHA is computed strictly from the uncompressed byte content of the 3D geometry file (SHA-1("blob " + size + "\0" + bytes)).

  4. Invariance Guarantee: Whether you make 1 commit or 10,000 commits to documentation, website pages, or Swift calculator code, the Git Blob Hash for that physical part never changes. It is 100% frozen in time until someone actually alters that specific CAD model.

  5. Path-Scoped CAD Commits (git log -1 -- <file>):

  6. When referencing authoring Git commits, the tooling queries the exact file: git log -1 --format="%h" -- Education/scad/fraction_studio_box.scad.

  7. Commits elsewhere in the monorepo do not alter this commit stamp. It only advances when that component's CAD code is modified.

  8. Part Identification Syntax:

  9. Standard Part ID format: <KIT_CODE>-<COMPONENT_SLUG>-<BLOB_SHA> (e.g., FRAC-FRAC-eba4c3e, SC-CHAS-436ba32).
  10. Customers can quote either the full Part ID, the debossed 7-character Git Blob Hash (eba4c3e), or the CAD commit (a793ddd).
  11. Automated Manifest Tool (Tools/generate_part_manifest.py): 
    # Regenerate the master part manifest and anti-arbitrage pricing:
python3 Tools/generate_part_manifest.py

# Reverse lookup any customer Git Blob Hash, commit, or component:
python3 Tools/generate_part_manifest.py --lookup eba4c3e
    The lookup instantly prints the component name, exact immutable Git blob SHA, CAD source commit, amortized cost, 50% anti-arbitrage price, and exact Git export command (git cat-file -p <blob_sha> > component.stl).

docs.title: 4.3 The Etsy Replacement Parts Workflow
docs.text:
1. Customer Order: A customer who lost a piece visits our dedicated Etsy listing (SC-REPLACE-01).
  2. Personalization Box: The buyer provides 3 details:
  3. Target Set (e.g. Fraction Studio, Algebra Factoring, SC-32)
  4. Missing Part & Color (e.g. 1/8 Eighth Block in Azure Blue, Linear x Rod in Coral)
  5. Part ID or Git Hash: Matched directly from the Archival Reference Card included inside their kit's box lid (or the underside inspection plaque on the box/chassis, e.g. FRAC-01-eba4c3e or a793ddd).
  6. Automated CAD Slicing: The fulfillment technician runs python3 Tools/generate_part_manifest.py --lookup <ID>, checks out the exact historical OpenSCAD commit, and slices on textured PEI.
  7. 24-Hour Dispatch: The replacement part is dispatched in a rigid stay-flat mailer envelope via standard USPS First Class mail with flat tracking.

docs.title: 5. Battery-Free Shipping Compliance Policy
docs.text: [!IMPORTANT] Strict Postal Compliance: NO BATTERIES SHIPPED IN ANY PACKAGE. In compliance with USPS Publication 52 (Hazardous Materials), FAA safety regulations, and IATA Class 9 (UN 3090 / UN 3091) air transport restrictions, StackCalc does not include lithium coin cell batteries in physical calculator shipments.

docs.title: Operational Rationale & Benefits:
docs.text:
1. Zero Hazmat Labeling & Airmail Friction: Lithium cells trigger complex DOT/USPS Section 349 shipping rules, hazardous materials declarations, package labeling mandates, and restrictions on international priority airmail.
  2. Eliminated Fire & Ingestion Liability: Eliminates Reese's Law (16 CFR Part 1263) pre-installed battery testing certification requirements for shipping packages.
  3. Universal Accessibility: The SC-32 uses a standard, ubiquitous CR2032 3V coin cell available at any grocery store, pharmacy, or hardware store for ~$0.50.
  4. Transparent Customer Notice: Every calculator listing and package insert clearly states: "Requires 1x standard CR2032 coin cell (widely available, omitted from shipment per postal carrier safety regulations)."

docs.title: 8. Multi-Marketplace Visual Asset Strategy & Blender Physics Pipeline
docs.text: StackCalc products are syndicated across Etsy, Amazon Handmade, eBay, and our direct website (stackcalc.io). Each channel requires distinct visual asset standards:

docs.title: 1. Amazon Main Image Compliance Standard (Pure White #FFFFFF)
docs.text:
• TOS Requirement: Amazon Seller Central and Handmade policies require MAIN listing images to feature a 100% pure white background (RGB 255, 255, 255 / #FFFFFF). Images with off-white backgrounds, props, or text overlays are algorithmically suppressed.
  • Implementation (setup_amazon_white_background):
  • World background set to (1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0).
  • Floor plane set as Cycles is_shadow_catcher = True to preserve soft, natural contact ambient occlusion shadows without dirtying the white level.
  • Product occupies 85–90% of the frame with zero graphic text overlays.

docs.title: 2. 3D-Modeled Environments (Strictly NO AI Generation)
docs.text:
• Why AI Images are Rejected: Generative AI tools (Midjourney/Flux/Photoshop) hallucinate geometry, scramble debossed mathematical notation, create impossible gear tooth profiles, and trigger deep skepticism among discerning STEM teachers and engineers.
  • The 3D PBR Environment Standard: All contextual lifestyle scenes are rendered directly in Blender Cycles using our authentic OpenSCAD CAD models resting inside photorealistic 3D-modeled environments:
  • Procedural Scandinavian blonde and honey oak desk surfaces (create_smooth_oak_desk_material).
  • Physical drafting tools (aluminum millimeter rulers, self-healing cutting mats).
  • Subtle depth-of-field (f/3.2 camera aperture) softly blurring classroom background elements while keeping CAD chamfers razor-sharp.

docs.title: 3. Bullet Physics Simulation Mandate (Zero Intersecting Boxes)
docs.text:
• Problem: Hardcoded static coordinates often result in loose blocks or tiles penetrating tray sidewalls or clipping through box lips.
  • Mandate: All multi-object Blender scenes must invoke simulate_rigid_body_settling(scene, passive_objs, active_objs):
  • Containers (Gridfinity boxes, calculation stages, desk surfaces) are configured as PASSIVE rigid bodies with MESH collision shapes.
  • Loose components (polynomial tiles, fraction blocks, counters, dice) are configured as ACTIVE rigid bodies with CONVEX_HULL shapes.
  • The physics engine steps 35 frames under standard gravity (\(g = -9810\,\text{mm/s}^2\)) with dampening until equilibrium is reached.
  • Visual transforms are permanently baked (matrix_world.copy()) prior to Cycles rendering, guaranteeing physically valid, non-intersecting geometry.

docs.title: 9. Real Physical Product Photography & Digital Darkroom Pipeline
docs.text: While CAD raytracing and physics settling provide ideal architectural consistency, real physical photographs of authentic 3D printed parts dramatically outperform synthetic images in conversion rate (CRO). Savvy Etsy shoppers, STEM teachers, and school procurement officers actively look for real physical surface textures, genuine matte PEI bed patterns, authentic layer adhesion, and debossed inspection marks.

docs.title: 9.1 The "Zero AI Hallucination" Standard
docs.text:
• Strict Prohibition: Never use text-to-image generative AI (e.g. Midjourney, Flux, Imagen) to create commercial hero shots. Generative AI hallucinates impossible geometry, distorts debossed typography, and erodes customer trust.
  • The Physical Digital Darkroom: All commercial studio shots must be generated directly from authentic, bench-photographed hardware using computer vision and digital darkroom processing (Tools/rendering/enhance_real_photos.py).

docs.title: 9.2 The 5-Stage Retouching & Staging Workflow
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────┐     1. D65 White Balance       ┌─────────────────────────┐
│ Raw Bench Photograph    │ ────────────────────────────► │ Neutral Color Temp      │
│ (Yellow Tungsten Cast)  │     (Gray-world algorithm)     │ (Maple/PEI Restored)    │
└─────────────────────────┘                                └────────────┬────────────┘
                                                                        │
                                2. CLAHE Luminance Micro-Contrast       ▼
                                ────────────────────────────────► ┌─────────────────────────┐
                                (Highlights debossed letters &    │ Matte Texture Pop       │
                                 fuzzy-skin tactile ridges)       │ (Clean Dark Charcoal)   │
                                                                  └────────────┬────────────┘
                                                                               │
                                3. GrabCut Foreground Extraction               ▼
                                ────────────────────────────────► ┌─────────────────────────┐
                                (Feathered sub-pixel alpha mask)  │ Isolated Real Box       │
                                                                  └──────┬───────────┬──────┘
                                                                         │           │
                     4A. Ground Contact Shadow Projection                │           │ 4B. Desk Staging
       ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘           │
       ▼                                                                             ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐                       ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Pure White (#FFFFFF) Studio     │                       │ Classroom Desk In-Situ          │
│ • Amazon/eBay/Etsy main shot    │                       │ • Textured wooden study desk    │
│ • Multi-stage contact AO shadow │                       │ • Soft f/2.8 background bokeh   │
│ • Razor-sharp physical print    │                       │ • Natural warm wood reflections │
└─────────────────────────────────┘                       └─────────────────────────────────┘
  1. D65 Daylight Normalization: Corrects the typical indoor warm tungsten or fluorescent color cast back to neutral daylight (6500K), ensuring accurate plastic and desk color representation.
  2. Micro-Contrast & Texture Extraction: Applies Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) on the LAB luminance channel (\(L^*\)) to elevate subtle debossed lettering (TEN FRAMES, StackCalc), layer lines, and fuzzy-skin matte textures without washing out contrast.
  3. Sub-Pixel Alpha Segmentation: Uses OpenCV GrabCut with elliptical morphological closing and Gaussian edge feathering to isolate the real 3D printed box without stray halos or burrs.
  4. Physically Grounded Contact Shadows: Eliminates "floating box" artifacts by extracting the real ground contact polygon (\([x_{min}, y_{contact}]\) to \([x_{max}, y_{contact}]\)) and rendering a multi-stage ambient occlusion shadow (tight dark contact line + soft diffused floor penumbra).
  5. Multi-Marketplace Compositing:
  6. Amazon / eBay / Etsy Main Image: Scaled and centered with 12–15% breathing room on pure white (#FFFFFF).
  7. Contextual In-Situ Image: Composited onto high-resolution 3D-modeled classroom oak desks with optical depth-of-field blur.
  8. Retouched Bench Hero: Full-resolution original workshop photo with professional lighting, contrast curve, and lens vignette.

docs.title: Detailed Regulatory Explanations
docs.text:
1. Absence of Wireless Communication Radios: The SC-32 mainboard uses a bare-metal Raspberry Pi RP2350 microcontroller with zero radio peripherals. There are no antenna traces, Bluetooth modules, Wi-Fi chips, or infrared data links on the PCB. It is physically incapable of transmitting or receiving wireless signals.

  2. Strict Numerical Engine (No Symbolic CAS): Prohibited CAS calculators can simplify algebraic expressions symbolically (e.g. factoring \(x^2 - 9\) into \((x-3)(x+3)\) or taking symbolic derivatives \(\frac{d}{dx}\sin(x) = \cos(x)\)). StackCalc does not feature a CAS. Its solvers evaluate strictly numerical roots (via secant/Brent numerical methods) and numerical integrals (via Romberg quadrature), identical to classic approved scientific calculators.

  3. Standard Scientific Keypad: The keypad contains 43 tactile keys arranged in an industry-standard scientific matrix with numerical and transcendental legends. Keys do not follow typewriter (QWERTY) arrangements.

  4. Continuous Memory Reset Protocol: Before entering an exam center, test proctors can request students clear continuous memory. To clear all memory in seconds:

  5. Press Left Shift + C (CLEAR).
  6. Press CLSTK to purge all 4 operational stack levels (\(X, Y, Z, T\)).
  7. Press CLREGS to purge all 26 storage registers (\(R_0 \dots R_{25}\)).
  8. Press CLSTAT to purge statistical accumulations.

docs.title: 4. Frequently Asked Questions by Exam Proctors
docs.text:
Is Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) allowed on the SAT or ACT?

Yes. Neither The College Board nor ACT prohibits Reverse Polish Notation. Both organizations regulate calculator capabilities (disallowing QWERTY keyboards, wireless communication, and symbolic CAS), not the internal stack entry logic. RPN calculators have been officially permitted on collegiate and secondary exams for over 45 years.

Can students store formulas in continuous memory?

The SC-32 includes 26 general-purpose numerical storage registers (\(R_0 \dots R_{25}\)) for intermediate floating-point numbers. It does not possess a text editor, notes app, or file storage system. Proctors can verify a clean state by having students execute the CLEAR → CLREGS routine upon entering the examination hall.

Does the calculator have a sound or audio beeper that could distract other examinees?

No. The SC-32 contains no speaker, buzzer, or piezo element. Keystrokes are completely silent mechanical tactile clicks (400g snap-dome actuation).

docs.title: Embedded Swift firmware
docs.text:
StackCalc's firmware source targets the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 / RP2350 using Embedded Swift and a C hardware layer. It shares calculator logic and the bitmap interface with RPNCore.

The pictured physical calculator is an unpowered mechanical prototype. Board fabrication and integration are still in progress. The architecture below describes the current source, not measured performance of an assembled product. The public mechanical download does not include firmware source or a flashable release.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Source component Responsibility Main.swift Calculator event loop, input dispatch, display updates and continuous memory hardware_wrapper.c / BridgingHeader.h Pico SDK boundary for GPIO, SPI, time and flash RPNCore Shared calculator operations, key mapping, bitmap rendering and tutorials CMakeLists.txt Embedded build configuration; excludes app-only plotting Simulator/ Browser display and transport around the emulated firmware image

The physical design uses the current 37-key layout. Source sharing supports consistent behavior, but cross-platform parity must be checked with matching operations and state; it is not a blanket bit-for-bit guarantee for every feature.

docs.title: Display and input
docs.text:
The logical display is 132×65 pixels, with 1,188 bytes arranged as nine pages of 132 columns. The final page has one visible row. The hardware wrapper currently configures 8 MHz SPI and sends each page with blocking writes. It does not implement the previously described DMA or establish a tear-free display claim. Module/controller identity and physical edge visibility still need checking against the installed specimen and BOM.

The GPIO scanner samples the matrix; the Swift loop debounces changed input before dispatching the corresponding operation. The active loop uses a 10 ms sleep interval. In the source's sleeping state, the LCD output is disabled, scanning is restricted to C/ON, and the loop uses a 100 ms interval. Other keys do not wake that state. These source intervals are not measured touch-to-display latency or battery-life results.

docs.title: Continuous memory
docs.text:
The flash implementation alternates between two slots, each eight flash sectors, at the end of flash. It validates payloads with an FNV-1a checksum and selects the newer valid sequence. It also includes migration from the older, smaller slot layout.

This replaces the earlier description of two 4 KB sectors and CRC32. Power-loss recovery, flash endurance and retention must be evaluated on the matching board. The firmware uses allocated buffers and Swift collections; zero heap allocation is not a current claim.

docs.title: Build and inspection
docs.text:
These commands are for a source checkout with the configured Embedded Swift toolchain, Pico SDK, ARM compiler, CMake and Ninja. The current local Pico SDK checkout is based on 2.3.0. The build script accepts WATCHCALC_SWIFT_TOOLCHAIN for an external Swift toolchain and otherwise uses Firmware/toolchains/swift.

Run from the repository root:

# Hardware UF2
Firmware/compile_firmware.sh hardware

# Instrumented hardware build
Firmware/compile_firmware.sh profile

# Firmware image for the localhost emulator
Firmware/compile_firmware.sh emulator
node Firmware/Simulator/server.js

# ELF sizing and optional live hardware counters
python3 Firmware/profile_power_memory.py

Each build replaces Firmware/build; run the variants sequentially. The hardware output is Firmware/build/WatchCalcFirmware.uf2, copied to Hardware/output/WatchCalc32_Manufacturing/Firmware_Files/WatchCalcFirmware_RP2350.uf2. The profile variant uses the _Profile.uf2 suffix in that export directory. An emulator build is for the simulator, not for flashing a board.

docs.title: Physical verification still required
docs.text:
A powered board is needed to verify cold startup, input-to-display timing, display edges, memory recovery, current consumption and battery life. The previous sub-15 ms boot, sub-two-second flashing and multi-month battery statements were not qualified measurements and are withdrawn.

When a board-specific firmware release is available, its instructions must identify the board revision, matching UF2, USB/BOOTSEL access and recovery procedure. Do not infer those details from the mechanical prototype photos.

See the hardware build and capability reference for the current mechanical kit and its qualification limits.

docs.title: Assembly and service
docs.text: Dry-fit the matching faceplate and membrane in the chassis rails, then fit the snap-retained cap. The current release is an unpowered mechanical prototype: its RP2350 board design is in fabrication and is not installed in the pictured specimen. Once the board arrives, the integration sequence will add board seating, display alignment, switch reach, connector clearance, battery polarity, and power checks. Release the retention features rather than prying on the display surround when reopening the printed assembly.

docs.title: Material, Color & Faceplate Specification
docs.text:
[!IMPORTANT] Enclosure Color Clarification: Physical calculator enclosures are never white. All physical StackCalc production handhelds (SC-32 and SC-6) are molded and printed in dark, technical, high-rigidity thermoplastics (Sunlu Midnight Navy PLA 2.0+, Technical Matte Black PLA/PETG, Elegoo Space Gray PLA, Sunlu Dark Chestnut PLA, and Sunlu Coffee Brown PLA).

docs.text:
Before selecting the current TPU membrane direction, we printed integrated spring and key experiments to study travel, return behavior, and print tolerance in a single part. These experiments informed the mechanical layout, but they are not the current keypad design or a validation of final key force.

A printed test array with integrated circular key and spring features. It records an exploratory route that was superseded by the current TPU membrane direction.

Close view of the printed spring geometry. The current design work uses a separate TPU membrane; repeatable force, life, and tactile measurements remain future test work.

docs.title: 3. Deliberate Quality-of-Life Departures from Classic Handhelds
docs.text:
While maintaining functional pedigree, StackCalc incorporates deliberate modern enhancements to improve usability, durability, and educational clarity:

  1. Unified RPN Programming:
  2. Classic Handhelds: Required users to navigate between an archaic algebraic equation mode and keystroke programming.
  3. StackCalc: Unifies all equation definition into deterministic RPN stack operations. This eliminates parser ambiguities and ensures identical execution behavior on microcontrollers, phones, and watches.
  4. Dedicated Absolute Value (|x|) Key:
  5. Classic Handhelds: Hid the absolute value function deep within secondary menus.
  6. StackCalc: Assigns |x| directly to Right Shift +/-, providing instant one-touch evaluation.
  7. Modern Remainder Notation (÷R):
  8. Classic Handhelds: Labeled integer division ambiguously as INT÷.
  9. StackCalc: Uses ÷R to clearly communicate integer division with remainder, aligning with modern engineering and educational standards.
  10. Integrated Basic Plotting Engine (PLOT):
  11. Classic Handhelds: Required bulky peripheral thermal printers or external plotters to visualize data.
  12. StackCalc: Built-in plotting engine renders function evaluation curves (\(y = f(x)\)) and statistical scatter/regression plots directly on the transflective graphic LCD display and mobile screens.
  13. Clean Power Architecture (Software Targets):
  14. Classic Handhelds: Included a physical OFF key label.
  15. StackCalc: Retains power management on the hardware unit, but hides unnecessary power buttons on iOS and watchOS where operating system lifecycle handlers manage state.
  16. Configurable Stack Depth:
  17. Classic Handhelds: Restricted permanently to a 4-level stack (\(X, Y, Z, T\)).
  18. StackCalc: The FLAGS menu allows selecting between classic 4-level, 8-level, and unbounded Infinite stack depths.

docs.title: Apple Ecosystem & Desktop App: Mac, iPad, iPhone & Watch
docs.text:
StackCalc is engineered from day one as a unified physical-digital system. Our companion applications for macOS, iPadOS, iOS, and watchOS share the exact same deterministic Swift package—RPNCore—as our bare-metal Raspberry Pi RP2350 microcontroller firmware.

The apps share calculator semantics through RPNCore; platform capabilities and completed native regression evidence determine supported behavior.

docs.title: 1. Apple Watch: Pitch-Black Rapid Field
docs.text:
The watchOS application is designed for instant, glanceable number crunching directly on your wrist:

  • True OLED #000000 Background: Preserves battery life and blends invisibly with Apple Watch Series 10/11 edges.
  • Edge-Glow Wayfinding Beacons: Directional boundary pulses (Burnt Orange on the left, Blue on the right, Cyan on top) guide your finger across the keypad without looking.
  • Macro Screen-Tap ENTER: Tap anywhere on the upper display to execute an instant stack-lift ENTER without targeting a tiny button.
  • Continuous Tactile Feedback: Powered by Apple's Taptic Engine to simulate physical snap-dome switches.

docs.title: 2. iPhone & iPad: The 10-Column Landscape Layout
docs.text:
On iPad and iPhone, StackCalc expands into a spacious landscape and portrait instrument inspired by classic 1980s landscape scientific computing layouts:

  • 12-Character Segmented LCD: Emulates the authentic EastRising ST7567 transflective display with bundled Terminus typography.
  • Continuous Tactile Field (HPTC): Zero-distance drag gestures let you slide across key seams with subtle boundary clicks, sinking into button centers for heavy mechanical actuations.
  • Expandable TUI Overlays: Complex operations like Plotting, Integration, Equation Editing, and Tutorials smoothly expand into an authentic Text User Interface terminal.

docs.title: 3. macOS Desktop App: Physical Keyboard Ergonomics & Multi-Register Studio
docs.text:
On Mac, StackCalc becomes an indispensable engineering workstation instrument for macOS:

  • Native macOS Binary: Universal build optimized for Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) and Intel Macs, launching with zero startup latency.
  • Physical Keyboard & Numpad Mapping: Full physical keyboard ergonomics. The numeric keypad Enter executes RPN stack commit, standard arithmetic keys (+, -, *, /) trigger operations, Space or Return lifts the stack, and arrow keys cycle through registers.
  • Side-by-Side Multi-Register Inspector: On desktop monitors, expand the auxiliary side panel to inspect all operational stack levels (\(X, Y, Z, T\)), global storage registers (\(R_0 \dots R_{25}\)), and statistical accumulation registers (\(\Sigma\)) simultaneously.
  • Menu Bar Quick Calculator: Global keyboard shortcut summons a lightweight RPN scratchpad directly from the macOS menu bar for rapid calculations while writing code or LaTeX documents.

docs.text:
• 132:65 Reflective LCD: Reflective polarization matrix background (#E2E6EE) with dense carbon-black liquid crystal segments (#181A1B) delivering a 14.1:1 AAA contrast ratio.

docs.title: 5. Widget Architecture & Tutorial Integration
docs.text:
Watch uses one fixed black/orange/cyan functional scheme. iPhone, iPad and their widgets use the chosen material palette with direction and shape to identify shifts. System widget tint may override app colors. Ordinary widget arithmetic remains available beyond five taps; native pending feedback and an Open calculator route support handoff. Visible latency depends on the host and must be measured; no zero-latency guarantee is made.

Tutorials retain the phone calculator geometry. Watch guidance uses full-screen pages followed by its normal keypad. SC6 retains the tested vertical X/T display and correction behavior; a horizontal operand layout is not the current implementation.

docs.title: StackCalc Learning Lab
docs.text:
The Learning Lab is the physical STEM education ecosystem engineered by StackCalc. Rather than generic novelty toys, every manipulative in the Learning Lab is an authentic, tactile instrument designed to pair 1:1 with the physical keys and dedicated register displays of our SC-6 Elementary and SC-32 Scientific RPN calculators.

The calculator's high-contrast, four-line reflective LCD screen is the real operational stack. Students manipulate physical models on their desk, observe how values are staged, and verify calculations on the live stack registers without hidden parenthesis logic.

docs.title: The Physical Instrument Collection
docs.text:
All manipulatives are built on the open-source Gridfinity modular standard with tactile detents, dual-color filament lettering, debossed cartouche badges, and weighted rubber feet:

docs.title: Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract (CPA) Pedagogy
docs.text:
StackCalc directly implements Jerome Bruner’s CPA progression and Singapore Math methodologies:

  1. Concrete: Students physically construct quantities, group counters, rotate volvelles, or factor algebraic tiles.
  2. Pictorial: Students sketch representations, tape diagrams, or area models into their printed lab sheets.
  3. Abstract: Students push values onto the calculator's hardware stack ([ENTER]), apply operations, and inspect register state.

docs.title: Download Educational Literature & 3D Models

docs.title: Press Kit & Editorial Overview
docs.text:
StackCalc Calculator is a tactile, deterministic scientific RPN calculator and visual K–8 math companion for iPhone, iPad, and a 100% standalone Apple Watch app.

Rather than treating mobile math as another flat, soulless grid of glass—or hiding reasoning inside a black-box AI—StackCalc restores the physical joy, speed, and transparent step-by-step clarity of a dedicated mathematical instrument across one unified app with two built-in modes that grow with the learner from first grade through professional engineering.

docs.title: 2. The Design Philosophy: Bridging Classroom Intuition and Engineering Precision
docs.text:
Traditional math tools force learners through three disconnected worlds: children begin with physical classroom blocks, transition to algebraic school calculators cluttered with nested parentheses and syntax errors, and only encounter clean stack-based computation (Reverse Polish Notation) in university or professional engineering—often on discontinued vintage hardware like the HP-32SII or $250+ boutique collectors' calculators.

StackCalc was created to unify that journey in a single, accessible instrument:

  • End Parenthesis Anxiety: By keeping active numbers visible on a clean vertical stack, users operate on numbers in the exact order they think—eliminating bracket mismatches and hidden state.
  • Connect Physical and Digital Learning: Elementary students see numbers transform directly into visual models on screen alongside free, open-source 3D-printable classroom blocks, building spatial number sense before graduating to full scientific and calculus workflows.
  • Built for Everyday Use & Exam Integrity: Free of programming modes, CAS engines, QWERTY keyboards, ads, or subscriptions—delivering pure, distraction-free mathematical utility across iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch.

docs.title: 3. One Unified App, Two Built-In Modes
docs.text: StackCalc is a single universal app that adapts to the user's stage of learning through two purpose-built modes:

docs.title: Mode A: Scientific Mode (StackCalc 32) — The Modern HP-32SII Reimagined
docs.text:
Designed for engineers, scientists, AP students, and anyone who values speed and transparency over black-box answers:

  • Zero Parentheses, Visible 4-Level Stack (X, Y, Z, T): Enter numbers, tap operations, and watch intermediate results stay visible at every step. You never lose your place or battle syntax errors.
  • Exact Mixed Fractions (SIMP): Natural mixed-fraction entry and display (e.g., 2 1/8) with dedicated step-by-step prime factor reduction so students and builders see how fractions simplify.
  • Multi-Variable Equation Solver & Calculus: Store custom formulas, solve numerically for any unknown variable, and evaluate definite integrals using Simpson convergence.
  • Interactive Curve Plotting: High-contrast graphing canvas with real-time root inspection, inflection tracing, and shaded area-under-the-curve integration.
  • STEM & Computer Science Toolkit: Complex numbers, 2-variable statistical regressions, and Base-N programmer modes (HEX, DEC, OCT, BIN).

docs.title: Mode B: Visual Learning Mode (StackCalc 6 — New in Version 1.1)
docs.text:
In Version 1.1, switching into Visual Learning Mode (StackCalc 6) transforms the calculator into a distraction-free K–8 educational playground aligned with Singapore Math (Concrete • Pictorial • Abstract) and Common Core:

  • Live Pictorial LCD Visualizations: As students enter numbers and perform operations on a focused 2-level stack, the dot-matrix display dynamically renders quantities as:
  • Ten-Frames (10F): Subitizing and make-ten bridging strategies up to 100.
  • 20-Bead Number Rack (RACK): Classic 5-and-5 Rekenrek bead grouping for doubles and near-doubles fluency.
  • Dynamic Number Line (LINE): Proportional jump arcs illustrating addition and subtraction trajectories.
  • Analog Judy Clock (🕒): Synchronized hour, minute, and ticking second hands with elapsed time conversion.
  • Ratio, Stats & Frequency Tables: Side-by-side tabular inspection for elementary data literacy.
  • 5-Level Adaptive Fluency Quiz Engine (?): Generates targeted mental math challenges (L1–L5) that adapt to student response speed and accuracy, complete with live score tracking and celebratory mastery banners.

docs.title: A. 100% Standalone Apple Watch Instrument
docs.text:
Unlike companion calculator apps that rely on a paired iPhone or reduce the wrist to a basic four-function pad, StackCalc runs its complete scientific RPN math engine natively on watchOS:

  • 75% Direct Display-as-ENTER: The top 75% of the watch screen acts as an authoritative, no-look ENTER target—allowing effortless one-handed calculation in a lab, workshop, or field environment.
  • Digital Crown & Bezel Stack Scrubbing: Drag up from the lower 25% bezel or turn the Digital Crown to inspect all four stack registers (X, Y, Z, T) and scrub interactive tutorials.
  • True #000000 OLED Canvas & Wayfinding Beacons: Subtle directional color beacons (Burnt Orange, Electric Blue, Cyan) orient your thumb across key pages without visual clutter, paired with native Watch Face Complications and Smart Stack widgets.

docs.title: B. Continuous Tactile Field (CoreHaptics)
docs.text: Physical calculators are revered for the crisp snap of their keys. StackCalc’s custom CoreHaptics engine simulates both key-seam boundary pulses (so your finger can feel button edges when sliding across glass) and mechanical snap-dome actuation with distinct physical weight for numbers, shift modifiers, and ENTER.

docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text:
// LEGAL PROTOCOL · ZERO DATA COLLECTION · EFFECTIVE SEPTEMBER 14, 2026

At StackCalc, we believe mathematics is personal, foundational, and should never be accompanied by surveillance, telemetry, or advertising. Whether you are using StackCalc32 on iOS, iPadOS, or Apple Watch, or following the physical calculator project, we collect zero personal data.

docs.title: 1. Zero Data Collection
docs.text:
• No Personal Information: We do not collect names, email addresses, phone numbers, physical addresses, or any personally identifiable information (PII).
  • No Analytics or Telemetry: We do not track keystrokes, calculation frequency, app session length, feature adoption, or user workflows.
  • No Device Identifiers: We do not read or transmit IDFA (Identifier for Advertisers), IDFV (Identifier for Vendors), MAC addresses, or IP addresses.
  • No Diagnostics or Crash Reports: We do not bundle third-party crash tracking or diagnostic SDKs.
  • No Biometrics or Health Data: While running standalone on Apple Watch, StackCalc does not access Apple Health, heart rate sensors, workout data, or any biometric sensors.

docs.title: 2. 100% Local On-Device Computation
docs.text:
Every calculation, stack operation, variable memory register, equation, and statistical curve is evaluated exclusively within the local memory of your device:

  • RPN Stack & Memory Registers: Stack levels (X, Y, Z, T, and extended levels), storage registers (0–9, A–Z), and financial registers are stored in local device memory only.
  • Continuous Memory: In accordance with physical calculator behavior, values stored in continuous memory remain preserved locally between app sessions until manually cleared (CLEAR → Continuous Memory) or until the application is removed from your device.
  • No Cloud Synchronization: The application operates completely offline. No network connectivity is required, requested, or used.

docs.title: 3. Third-Party Services & SDKs
docs.text: The application contains zero third-party software development kits (SDKs), tracking pixels, ad networks, or third-party APIs. We do not sell, rent, monetize, or disclose any user data to third parties under any circumstance.

docs.title: 4. Children’s Online Privacy Protection (COPPA & Global Standards)
docs.text:
StackCalc is designed for learners of all ages, from elementary school students exploring exact fraction manipulatives to university students and professionals performing advanced scientific analysis.

  • Because we do not collect any personal data from any user, we strictly comply with the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and California privacy laws.
  • We do not require account creation, registration, or login.
  • Children can safely use StackCalc in classrooms, exams, and at home without privacy risk.

docs.title: 5. Website Privacy (stackcalc.io)
docs.text:
Our documentation and storefront website (https://www.stackcalc.io) is hosted via GitHub Pages. Standard server access logs (such as IP addresses and browser user-agent headers) may be automatically processed by GitHub to ensure infrastructure security and deliver the web service. We do not inject tracking cookies or third-party marketing trackers on this documentation site.

StackCalc does not currently process direct physical-product purchases through this website. If a future product links to a named marketplace, that marketplace's privacy policy will describe its checkout, payment, and shipping-data practices.

docs.title: 6. Data Retention and Deletion
docs.text:
Because StackCalc collects no data on remote servers:

  • There is no remote account or database record to delete.
  • To erase all local state, press Yellow Shift + C (CLEAR) → tap CLALL inside the app, or uninstall the application from your Apple device.

docs.title: 7. Changes to This Policy
docs.text: We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect future updates or legal compliance. Any changes will be posted immediately to this URL (https://www.stackcalc.io/privacy/) with an updated effective date.

docs.title: 1. The \(135\,\text{mm} \times 90\,\text{mm}\) Golden Reference Card Standard
docs.text:
Every physical StackCalc product kit includes a custom duplex Archival Reference & Video QR Card. The card acts as a protective cover over the nested Gridfinity tray and provides the customer with an immediate visual schematic and instructional entry point upon lifting the box lid.

SIDE A: FRONT (TOP-FACING)

docs.title: Dimensional Engineering & Fit Rationale
docs.text: Dimension Specification Engineering Justification Width \(135.0\,\text{mm}\) Fits within \(150\,\text{mm} \times 150\,\text{mm}\) laser engraving working beds with \(7.5\,\text{mm}\) perimeter clamping margin. Height \(90.0\,\text{mm}\) Fits inside standard \(6 \times 4 \times 2\text{ in}\) (\(152 \times 102\,\text{mm}\)) corrugated mailers with \(8.5\,\text{mm}\) finger extraction clearance. Corner Radius \(r = 3.0\,\text{mm}\) Eliminates dog-earing, paper cuts, and friction snags inside corrugated boxes. Aspect Ratio \(1.50 : 1\) (\(3 : 2\)) Golden ratio matching standard photographic index plates and postcard standards. Gridfinity Overlap Spans 3x1 (\(125.5\,\text{mm}\)) and 3x2 (\(125.5 \times 84\,\text{mm}\)) Sits flush on top of organizer bins as an integrated dust shield and presentation layer.

docs.title: Pathway A: High-Speed Laser Printer Paper (Bulk School District Orders)
docs.text:
• Target Orders: Classroom 10-packs, 30-packs, and school district purchase orders.

  • Toner Strategy: Clean white background (#FFFFFF) with high-contrast midnight charcoal typography (#0F172A).
  • Why avoid full black flood? Flooding paper with black toner causes thermal curl, ink flaking on folds, and smudge risk during humid classroom use.
  • Zero-Cut Feeding Solution: Feed pre-cut \(4 \times 6\text{ in}\) (\(101.6 \times 152.4\,\text{mm}\)) or \(3.5 \times 5\text{ in}\) (\(88.9 \times 127\,\text{mm}\)) blank index cardstock into the laser printer's manual bypass tray, completely eliminating manual scissors or paper trimmer labor.
  • Throughput: ~30 double-sided cards per minute.

docs.title: Pathway B: Precision Laser-Engraved Black Card (SC-32 & Retail Kits)
docs.text:
• Target Orders: SC-32 scientific calculator, keynote showcase editions, and direct retail.
  • Substrate: 300 gsm black matte cardstock (with white core) or \(1.0\,\text{mm}\) black anodized aluminum / black cast acrylic.
  • Color Constraint: Strictly Monochrome White on Black (#FFFFFF on #000000). Laser ablation vaporizes the black top coat to reveal crisp white substrate underneath.
  • Single-Pass Automation (Zero Manual Cutting):
  • The laser engraves the exploded wireframe, Part ID manifest, California QC badge, and Side B vector QR code.
  • In the same job without moving the substrate, the laser vector-cuts the outer \(135.0 \times 90.0\,\text{mm}\) boundary with \(r = 3.0\,\text{mm}\) rounded corners.
  • Finished, deburred cards drop out ready for packaging—zero manual labor.
  • Throughput: ~90 seconds per double-sided card.

docs.title: 1. How does RPN (Stack Math) work? Why are there no parentheses?
docs.text:
In Reverse Polish Notation (RPN), operators follow their operands: - To evaluate \(5 + 3\): Press 5, ENTER, 3, +. - To evaluate \((4 \times 5) + (6 \times 7)\): Press 4, ENTER, 5, ×, 6, ENTER, 7, ×, +.

RPN completely eliminates parentheses, eliminates syntax errors, and keeps all intermediate calculation steps visible in the 4-level stack (X, Y, Z, T).

docs.title: 2. How do I display and calculate with exact fractions?
docs.text: StackCalc includes an arbitrary-precision rational fractions engine: - To toggle between decimal representation and exact fractional notation, press Left Shift + . (FDISP). - A decimal like 2.125 instantly renders as exact 2 1/8. - Pressing . between integers enters mixed fractions directly (e.g., 3 . 1 /c 2 for \(3 \frac{1}{2}\)).

docs.title: 3. Does the Apple Watch app require an iPhone nearby?
docs.text: No. StackCalc for watchOS is a 100% standalone instrument. - The entire calculation engine runs locally on the watch's processor. - You can perform full 4-level stack calculations, statistical summations, and trigonometric analysis directly on your wrist with zero phone connectivity. - Features high-contrast typography, digital crown scrubbing, and continuous edge-glow tactile haptic pulses.

docs.title: 4. How do I switch between the Hardware Digital Twin and Modern App interfaces?
docs.text: StackCalc offers two distinct user interfaces on iPhone and iPad: - Hardware Replica (Default): An authentic, brutalist digital twin of our physical open-source hardware, featuring the high-contrast icy silver-blue ST7567A dot-matrix screen, trapezoidal snap-dome key caps, and laser-marked legends. - Modern App: An expansive, glassmorphism-free touch interface with dynamic softkeys and high-resolution TUI graph rendering. - To Switch Interface: Press Left Shift + FLAGS (or tap FLAGS in the menu catalog) → HW → select APP or REPLICA. - Faceplate Themes: You can also customize faceplate aesthetics in the same menu via FLAGS → FACE (RETRO, STEALTH, NOVA, SPACE, or VOYAGER).

docs.title: 5. How do I use the Equation Solver and Numerical Integrator?
docs.text: StackCalc includes an equation solver based on classic Romberg numerical integration and secant root-finding algorithms: 1. Press Right Shift + STO (EQN Mode) to view or input equations. 2. Select an equation (such as the preloaded Normal PDF NPDF). 3. Press SOLVE to solve for any independent variable without isolating it algebraically. 4. Press ∫ (Integrate) to perform numerical integration across specified upper and lower bounds.

docs.title: 6. How do I clear continuous memory or reset the calculator?
docs.text:
• Clear Current X Entry / Cancel: Press C (or backspace ←).
  • The CLEAR Menu: Press Left Shift + C (CLEAR) to open the dedicated memory reset menu:
  • CLSTK: Clears all four levels of the operational stack (\(X, Y, Z, T\)).
  • CLREGS: Clears the 26 storage registers (\(R_0 \dots R_{25}\)).
  • CLSTAT: Clears all two-variable statistical accumulation registers (\(\Sigma x, \Sigma y, \Sigma x^2, \Sigma y^2, \Sigma xy, n\)).
  • CLEQN: Clears all stored user equations.
  • CLVARS: Clears all variables and financial registers.
  • CLALL: Complete factory reset; clears all stack levels, variables, registers, and equations back to initial state.

docs.title: Learn by Doing: Interactive TUI Tutorials
docs.text:
The StackCalc32 firmware, Apple Watch app, and iOS app include 16 built-in interactive lessons powered by the native Text User Interface (TUI).

The TUI replaces standard nested modal dialogues with an expandable, chatbot-style scrolling terminal rendered in the bundled Terminus pixel font. Lessons describe physical and digital calculator operations, providing real-time verification against the deterministic RPNCore engine.

docs.title: 1. Terminal Navigation & Controls
docs.text:
Learn how to navigate the expandable TUI scrolling transcript buffer and switch between the standard 1-line LCD and the full-screen terminal.

> TUI: CONTROLS (LESSON 1/16) [C] EXIT

> Terminal navigation tutorial.

> Use ↰ + 8 to scroll up and ↰ + 7 to scroll down.

> Step 1: Press Left Shift (↰)

> Step 2: Press 8 [SCROLL UP]

> Step 3: Press Left Shift (↰)

> Step 4: Press 7 [SCROLL DOWN]

> VERIFIED: Transcript buffer navigation unlocked.

0.0000_ [NEXT]
  • Tap ↰ (Left Shift) to engage the shift annunciator.
  • Tap 8 to scroll up into previous calculation history.
  • Tap 7 to scroll down back to the active prompt.
  • Tap C to dismiss the TUI overlay back to the primary stack view.

docs.title: 2. RPN Basics: Eliminating Parentheses
docs.text:
Reverse Polish Notation replaces the traditional = button and parenthesis keys with an automatic 4-level stack (\(X, Y, Z, T\)).

Mission: Calculate \(5 + 3\) without parentheses.

> TUI: RPN BASICS (LESSON 2/16) [C] EXIT

> Mission: Calculate 5 + 3 with no parentheses.

> In RPN, you enter arguments first, then specify the operator.

> Step 1: Tap 5

> Step 2: Tap ENTER [Lifts 5 into Stack Register Y]

> Step 3: Tap 3 [Enters 3 into Stack Register X]

> Step 4: Tap + [Combines Y and X into X]

> VERIFIED: X = 8.0000 [STACK LIFT ARMED]

8.0000_ [NEXT]
  1. Tap 5: Types 5_ left-justified on the LCD display.
  2. Tap ENTER: Commits 5 to the bottom of the stack and arms stack-lift.
  3. Tap 3: Types 3_ in the active \(X\) register while \(Y\) retains 5.
  4. Tap +: Instantly evaluates \(5 + 3 = 8.0000\).

docs.title: 3. Complex Numbers: Euler’s Identity
docs.text:
StackCalc handles full complex pairs \((a + bi)\) natively across all scientific and transcendental functions.

Mission: Verify Euler's identity: \(e^{\pi i} = -1\).

> TUI: COMPLEX PAIRS (LESSON 3/16) [C] EXIT

> Mission: Verify e^(πi) = −1 with complex pairs.

> Step 1: Tap 0 -> press ENTER [Real part in Y = 0]

> Step 2: Tap Right Shift -> Tap SIN (π) [Imaginary part in X = 3.1416]

> Step 3: Tap Left Shift -> Tap STO (CMPLX) [Arms complex operator]

> Step 4: Tap eˣ [Evaluates transcendental e^(0 + πi)]

> Step 5: Left Shift -> STO (CMPLX) -> Right Shift -> ENTER (SHOW)

> VERIFIED: Result = −1.0000 + 0.0000i

-1.0000_ [NEXT]

docs.title: 4. Fraction Entry & Manual Simplification ([SIMP])
docs.text:
Unlike consumer calculators that automatically simplify fractions and hide the underlying math from students, StackCalc preserves exact fraction state. Students must press [SIMP] to actively reduce fractions step-by-step.

Mission: Enter \(\frac{2}{4}\) and reduce it to \(\frac{1}{2}\).

> TUI: FRACTION SIMPLIFICATION (LESSON 5/16) [C] EXIT

> Mission: Enter 2/4 and reduce step-by-step.

> Format: [Whole] . [Numerator] . [Denominator]

> Step 1: Tap . -> Tap 2 -> Tap . -> Tap 4 [.2.4]

> Step 2: Tap ENTER [Displays: .2.4_ without reducing]

> Step 3: Tap Softkey [SIMP]

> VERIFIED: Common divisor 2 factored out -> .1.2 (.1/2)

.1.2_ [NEXT]

docs.title: 5. Mixed Fraction Arithmetic & Decimal Toggle ([FDISP])
docs.text:
Add mixed numbers exactly and toggle instantly between exact fractional form and floating-point decimal.

Mission: Add \(1 \frac{1}{2} + 1 \frac{3}{4} = 3 \frac{1}{4} = 3.2500\).

> TUI: MIXED FRACTION ARITHMETIC (LESSON 6/16) [C] EXIT

> Mission: Add 1 1/2 + 1 3/4 exactly.

> Step 1: Tap 1 . 1 . 2 -> Press ENTER [1 1/2 in Y]

> Step 2: Tap 1 . 3 . 4 [1 3/4 in X]

> Step 3: Tap + [Exact sum evaluated: 3 1/4]

> Step 4: Tap [FDISP] to toggle to decimal representation.

> VERIFIED: 3.2500 [PRESS FDISP AGAIN TO RETURN TO 3_1/4]

3.2500_ [NEXT]

docs.title: 6. Time Value of Money (TVM Amortization)
docs.text:
The built-in financial solver handles loan payments, mortgages, savings plans, and balloon notes without requiring complex algebraic formulas.

Mission: Calculate the monthly payment on a $200,000 30-year fixed loan at 5.5% annual interest.

\[\text{Monthly Payment} = \frac{PV \cdot i}{1 - (1 + i)^{-N}}\] > TUI: TVM AMORTIZATION (LESSON 8/16) [C] EXIT

> Loan parameters: N=360 months, I%YR=0.4583% (5.5% ÷ 12), PV=$200,000

> Step 1: 360 -> [N] (Number of periods)

> Step 2: 5.5 -> [ENTER] -> 12 -> [÷] -> [I%YR] (Monthly periodic rate)

> Step 3: 200000 -> [PV] (Present loan value)

> Step 4: 0 -> [FV] (Future loan balance)

> Step 5: Press [PMT] to execute solver.

> VERIFIED: PMT = -$1,135.58 / month

-1,135.58_ [NEXT]

docs.title: 7. Statistical Sums & Standard Deviation
docs.text:
Accumulate 2-variable data pairs \((x, y)\) into continuous memory registers using [Σ+] to calculate means and sample standard deviations.

Mission: Enter sample data points \((2, 4)\) and \((4, 6)\), then solve mean and standard deviation.

> TUI: STATISTICS & STD DEV (LESSON 14/16) [C] EXIT

> Step 1: Tap Left Shift (↰) -> CLEAR -> Σ (Clears stat registers)

> Step 2: 4 [Y] -> ENTER -> 2 [X] -> Tap Σ+ [Accumulates n=1]

> Step 3: 6 [Y] -> ENTER -> 4 [X] -> Tap Σ+ [Accumulates n=2]

> Step 4: Tap Right Shift -> yˣ (x̄, ȳ) -> Mean X = 3.0000, Mean Y = 5.0000

> Step 5: Tap Right Shift -> ¹/x (s, σ) -> Sample StdDev = 1.4142

> VERIFIED: Standard deviation s = 1.4142

1.4142_ [EXIT]

docs.title: 8. Executing Tutorials on Physical Firmware (RP2350)
docs.text: StackCalc32's 16 guided lessons are not limited to touchscreens—they are implemented natively in bare-metal Embedded Swift running on the physical RP2350 microcontroller. The hardware provides an authentic, distraction-free environment to master RPN calculation.

docs.title: Hardware Launch Sequence
docs.text:
• Dedicated Launcher Key: Press Left Shift ([↰]) + [C] anywhere on the physical keypad to launch the built-in Interactive Tutorial Runner.
  • Instant Event Interception: The firmware event loop intercepts matrix scanning, suspends the standard operational stack, and loads the active tutorial state machine directly into the display buffer.

docs.title: Physical Display & Dynamic Softkeys
docs.text:
• ST7567A Transflective LCD: The 132×65 pixel monochrome display renders a 4-line terminal transcript using the sharp 6×8 pixel Terminus font. High contrast ensures clear legibility under harsh laboratory lighting or direct sunlight.
  • Tactile Softkey Integration: The top row of 6 tactile keys dynamically maps to contextual controls:
  • Key 1 ([PREV]): Revisit the previous instruction step.
  • Key 2 ([NEXT]): Advance to the next step once target preconditions are verified.
  • Key 5 ([SKIP]): Jump ahead to the subsequent lesson in the curriculum.
  • Key 6 ([EXIT]): Dismiss the tutorial session and immediately restore your active calculation stack.

docs.title: Real-Time Keystroke & Stack Verification
docs.text:
• When an instructional step prompts for an input sequence (for example, 5 [ENTER] 3 [+]), the firmware monitors physical switch actuations across the 43-key matrix.
  • Each switch closure evaluates against the deterministic RPNCore math engine.
  • Upon matching expected results, the LCD displays VERIFIED: [TEST PASSED] and enables the [NEXT] softkey to advance.

docs.title: Non-Volatile Flash Memory Persistence
docs.text:
• Progress across the 16 lessons is tracked via an internal bitmask stored in the RP2350's non-volatile QSPI flash memory (firmwareTutorialCompletionMask).
  • Your tutorial progress and mastery state persist across deep sleep, power cycles, and battery changes.

docs.title: The Complete 16-Lesson Curriculum
docs.text:
Every lesson is available with complete bit-for-bit parity across the physical hardware instrument, iPad, and Apple Watch:

# Lesson Title Target Capabilities Covered 01 RPN Basics Stack lift mechanics, eliminating parentheses, 4-level register manipulation (\(X, Y, Z, T\)) 02 Complex Numbers Cartesian \((a + bi)\) entry, complex transcendentals, Euler's identity (\(e^{\pi i} = -1\)) 03 Angular Modes Degree, Radian, and Gradian conversions and trigonometric evaluations 04 Register Storage Direct and indirect register addressing with [STO] and [RCL] 05 Fraction Entry Three-part .Whole.Numerator.Denominator fractional format 06 Manual Simplification Factoring common divisors step-by-step using the [SIMP] key 07 Mixed Arithmetic Exact fractional addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division 08 Fraction/Decimal Toggle Toggling instantly between exact rational fractions and floating-point decimal via [FDISP] 09 TVM Amortization Solving loan amortization parameters ([N], [I%YR], [PV], [PMT], [FV]) without algebraic formulas 10 Unit Conversions Metric and Imperial length, mass, volume, and temperature conversions 11 Integer Division Integer quotient and remainder arithmetic using [÷R] notation 12 Last X Recovery Error correction and argument reuse via [LASTX] 13 Time Conversions Decimal hours to Hours:Minutes:Seconds ([▸HR], [▸HMS]) 14 Base Modes Hexadecimal, Decimal, Octal, and Binary base conversions and 36-bit integer arithmetic 15 Two-Variable Statistics Accumulating coordinate data pairs with [Σ+] and [Σ-] 16 Standard Deviation Sample (\(s\)) and population (\(\sigma\)) standard deviations, weighted means ([s,σ], [x̄,ȳ], [x̄w])

docs.text:
Master the tutorials on dedicated tactile hardware, or practice on your iPhone and Apple Watch:

EXPLORE THE LEARNING LAB → DOWNLOAD COMPANION APP STORE

docs.title: View-Only OpenAPI 3.1 Specification & Structured JSON Datasets
docs.text:
MACHINE-READABLE SPECIFICATION // AGENT GATEWAY ● OPENAPI 3.1 • JSON • ZERO AUTH VIEW-ONLY SPECIFICATION OpenAPI 3.1 (JSON)

Full schema for agents and tools.
